papers.title: Influence of strut tapering and joint-node height on mechanical response of BCC lattices
papers.abstract: Abstract This study investigates the tensile response of body-centered cubic (BCC) lattice structures with tapered struts manufactured from Ti6Al4V powder using a laser-beam powder bed fusion (PBF-LB) process. It quantifies how the end diameter $$(d_\textrm{end}$$ ), mid-span diameter $$(d_\textrm{mid}$$ ), and joint-node height $$(h)$$ affect Young’s modulus $$(E$$ ), 0.2% proof stress $$(R_\mathrm{p0.2}$$ ), and ultimate tensile strength $$(R_\textrm{m}$$ ). Experimental tensile tests performed on lattice specimens were combined with simulations based on the finite element method (FEM). A parametric dataset was created using results from finite element simulations and used to develop response surface regression models. The elastic and early plastic responses estimated numerically showed high agreement with experimentally observed responses, whereas the post-peak regime exhibited larger discrepancies associated with progressive failure and fabrication-induced variability. Increases in $$d_\textrm{mid}$$ and $$d_\textrm{end}$$ led to higher E , $$R_\mathrm{p0.2}$$ , and $$R_\textrm{m}$$ , with the largest gains observed when both diameters increased simultaneously. This indicates a strong geometric interaction. Joint-node height showed a secondary and geometry-dependent influence. All developed regression models explained more than 99% of the variability in FEM-estimated $$E$$ , $$R_\mathrm{p0.2}$$ , and $$R_\textrm{m}$$ , capturing nonlinear diameter effects and their interaction. When compared with experimentally determined $$E$$ , $$R_\mathrm{p0.2}$$ , and $$R_\textrm{m}$$ , the models explained 85%, 90%, and 88% of the variability in experimentally determined mechanical properties, respectively. Overall, the proposed framework and the developed regression models may serve as useful tools for early-stage unit-cell geometry screening in lattice structures with tapered struts within the investigated design space, while broader experimental validation remains necessary.

summary_en.motivation: To quantify the influence of strut tapering and joint-node height on the tensile mechanical properties of BCC lattices made from Ti6Al4V by PBF-LB.
summary_en.method: Experimental tensile tests combined with finite element simulations were used to generate a parametric dataset and develop response surface regression models.
summary_en.result: Increasing mid-span and end diameters simultaneously provided the greatest improvements in Young's modulus and strengths, with joint-node height playing a secondary role.
summary_en.validation: The regression models explained over 85% of experimental variability in E, Rp0.2, and Rm, though post-peak behavior showed larger discrepancies.

papers.title: Enhancement of the Wear and Corrosion Performance of Laser Powder Bed Fusion Ti-6Al-4V via in-situ Laser Surface Remelting Under a Nitrogen Atmosphere
papers.abstract: Abstract Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) enables the fabrication of Ti-6Al-4V components with complex geometries for biomedical and aerospace applications; however, the as-built surfaces often require additional post-processing to meet wear and corrosion performance requirements. In this study, an in-situ nitrogen-assisted laser surface remelting step is integrated into the LPBF workflow to enhance near-surface performance without external coatings or secondary treatments. The effect of this process intervention on surface integrity and functional response is systematically evaluated. Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) reveals pronounced grain refinement and texture modification within the remelted surface layer, while Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy is employed solely as a qualitative tool to indicate nitrogen-related surface bonding. As a result of the remelting process under a nitrogen environment, significant improvements in functional performance are achieved, with the wear volume reduced by 54% and the nanohardness increased by 18–22% compared to the as-built condition. Electrochemical measurements further indicate enhanced corrosion resistance, reflected by a 14% reduction in corrosion current density (Icorr). These results demonstrate that in-situ laser remelting under a nitrogen atmosphere can serve as an effective manufacturing strategy for improving the surface durability of LPBF Ti-6Al-4V components.

papers.title: Investigating crystallographic parameters and their impact on mechanical properties of Ti6Al4V alloy from selective Laser melting
papers.abstract: Selective Laser Melting (SLM) is a highly adaptable additive manufacturing method notable for its feature accuracy and flexibility. Processing Ti-6Al-4V alloy using SLM is particularly advantageous because of the alloy's unique structural features and thermal characteristics, making it well-suited for demanding applications where lightweight design, strength, and durability are essential. However, prohibitively large number of process parameters and complex thermo-physical phenomenon significantly influence the microstructural features, which in turn affect the torsional performance of printed Ti-6Al-4V components. In this study, the crystallographic structural features behavior of SLM-processed Ti-6Al-4V alloy components was investigated for high-performance loading applications. X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis of the 3D-printed SLM Ti-6Al-4V alloy specimens revealed crystallite sizes ranging from 687 to 2376 nm along the printed surface in the horizontal position (XY plane) and from 500 to 3747 nm along the part-building direction (Z-axis). Due to the associated microstrain effect, the printed surfaces in the horizontal position exhibited a region of tensile strain (2.440 × 10 −4 ), whereas those parallel to the part-building direction exhibited region of compressive strain (−0.3057 × 10 −4 ) during layer deposition. The printed surfaces demonstrated a higher degree of crystallinity in the vertical-position (96.9%) while the horizontal position exhibited a more amorphous structure (67.5%), suggesting that greater crystalline region develops along the part-building direction of the SLM process. Furthermore, the tensile and torsional yield strengths in the horizontal orientation (550 MPa and 308 MPa, respectively) were slightly higher than those in the vertical directions (540 MPa and 306 MPa, respectively), indicating a marginally better mechanical resistance in the horizontally oriented features compared to the vertically oriented ones.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文聚焦于激光选区熔化Ti-6Al-4V合金的晶体学参数与力学性能（拉伸和扭转），符合方向L1对增材制造Ti-6Al-4V力学性能的要求。
llm.why_not_core: The paper does not address fatigue performance, S-N curves, or crack behavior, which are central to the fatigue focus of Layer 1, though it covers tensile and torsional mechanical properties.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究SLM工艺参数对Ti-6Al-4V合金晶体结构及力学性能的影响。
summary_zh.method: 通过XRD分析晶体尺寸和微应变，并进行拉伸和扭转力学测试。
summary_zh.result: 水平方向拉伸和扭转屈服强度略高于垂直方向，结晶度在垂直方向更高。
summary_zh.validation: 实验力学测试与XRD表征验证了晶体参数与性能的关系。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate how crystallographic parameters (crystallite size, microstrain, crystallinity) influence the mechanical properties of SLM-processed Ti-6Al-4V alloy.
summary_en.method: X-ray diffraction was used to quantify crystallite size and microstrain, and tensile and torsional tests were performed to evaluate mechanical properties in horizontal and vertical orientations.
summary_en.result: Horizontal orientation exhibited slightly higher tensile (550 MPa) and torsional (308 MPa) yield strengths than vertical (540 MPa and 306 MPa), and vertical orientation had higher crystallinity (96.9%) compared to horizontal (67.5%).
summary_en.validation: Experimental validation through mechanical testing and XRD analysis of printed specimens.

papers.title: Laser Powder Bed Fusion Processing of Ti-6Al-4V Powders with Offsize and Wide Particle Size Distributions—Process Optimization
papers.abstract: The considerable expense associated with metal additive manufacturing (AM), partly attributed to the high costs of raw materials, forms a significant obstacle hindering the widespread adoption and scaling of this technology. In response to this challenge, this study endeavors to explore and optimize the laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) process parameters for Ti-6Al-4V powders with offsize (45–106 µm) and wide (15–106 µm) particle size distribution (PSD) which are more cost-effective. The outcomes will be compared to those of the same alloy with a standard 15–53 µm PSD. The primary focus of this investigation revolves around two key objectives: firstly, establishing correlations between the laser powder bed fusion process parameters and the resulting density, hardness, and roughness. This objective is achieved by investigating the impact of process parameters within the context of the contour–skin–core method. Secondly, the porosity, microstructure, elemental composition, and dimensional fidelity of several components made from the offsize and wide powders were investigated, utilizing the optimized process parameters for density. To this end, an efficient multi-step experimental design and optimization process was adopted. The findings resulted in the identification of correlations between the significant process parameters and the studied responses, enabling the achievement of 98.7% density and 40.6 HRC hardness for offsize powder and 98.7% density and 40 HRC hardness for wide powder. A separate set of optimized process parameters for larger geometries produced densities exceeding 99.9% in both as-built and HIP conditions across all three powders. Additionally, the results confirmed the higher sensitivity of the roughness to powder size, with the optimized values fluctuating between 9.5 µm and 15.7 µm. Comprehensive microstructural investigation reveals no significant differences in phase evolution or grain structure resulting from the use of offsize or wide powders. This study confirms the viability of utilizing powders containing a higher portion of large particles to mitigate the costs associated with LPBF processes.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了非标粒径Ti-6Al-4V粉末的LPBF工艺优化，提供了硬度、密度等基础力学性能数据，但与疲劳性能无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not provide mechanical/fatigue properties such as tensile strength, ductility, or fatigue life; it focuses on process optimization for cost reduction rather than detailed mechanical characterization.

summary_zh.motivation: 降低粉末成本，优化非标粒径Ti-6Al-4V粉末的LPBF工艺参数。
summary_zh.method: 采用多步实验设计，优化轮廓-核心-表皮策略下的工艺参数，并对比标准粉末。
summary_zh.result: 获得密度>99.9%、硬度~40 HRC、粗糙度9.5-15.7 μm的成形件。
summary_zh.validation: 通过密度、硬度、显微组织表征验证工艺可行性。

summary_en.motivation: To reduce raw material costs by using offsize and wide particle size distribution Ti-6Al-4V powders in laser powder bed fusion.
summary_en.method: A multi-step experimental design optimized LPBF parameters within a contour–skin–core strategy, correlating parameters with density, hardness, and roughness.
summary_en.result: Densities exceeding 99.9% and hardness around 40 HRC were achieved for both as-built and HIP conditions, with roughness between 9.5 and 15.7 μm.
summary_en.validation: Experimental measurements of density, hardness, surface roughness, and microstructural analysis validated the results.
